citation.authors: Chen X, Wang R, Zee P et al

cited_by.title: Sleep, short sleep and sleep apnoea

record.population: 2,230 US adults aged 54 to 93 (MESA Sleep cohort), including Black participants
record.design: Cross-sectional study with overnight sleep tests and wrist monitors
record.finding: Compared with white adults, Black adults had higher odds of sleep apnoea syndrome (OR 1.78, 95% CI 1.20 to 2.63), short sleep under 6 hours (OR 4.95, 3.56 to 6.90), poor sleep quality (OR 1.57) and daytime sleepiness (OR 1.89). Only 7.4% to 16.2% of people with moderate or worse sleep-disordered breathing reported a prior diagnosis.
record.note: Cross-sectional, ages 54 to 93, US; adjusted for age, sex and site only.
